newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shrs end mixed, mkt skewed by cross trades.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shrs end mixed, mkt skewed by cross trades.

text.p: Most shares rose on the Caracas Stock Exchange as the market index slipped for the fourth successive session in a day skewed by cross trades and the absence of foreign investors, brokers said.
The market's 19-share index fell 0.19 percent at 4,584.69, as 16 stocks closed higher, 11 lower and eight unchanged.
"I think the market is being closely followed by foreign investors who, although they are waiting for news, are continuing to take positions," said Freddy Zambrano of the Interacciones brokerage.
A total of 4.342 billion bolivars ($9.1 million) worth of shares changed hands thanks largely to cross trades, or trades between portfolios within the same brokerage house.
"If you take out the cross trades, the volume was low," said Mario Simosa of the Multinvest brokerage.

Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas rose 3.00 bolivars to 394.00 bolivars, steel company Sivensa slipped 2.75 bolivars to 289.25 bolivars and agro-industrial company Mavesa rose 0.50 bolivar to 120.50.
